<details><summary>AI feedback</summary>
Not applied yet: D1 and D2. Open: Q1 and Q2.

D1: web-platform-tests/wpt#65371 doesn't test the `inert` case of the focusing steps, or an explicit `focus({ preventScroll: false })` on the element that already has focus (the case #4512 asks about). Not applied: [proposed fix](https://github.com/mrego/wpt/pull/554), two reftests that pass in Chrome Canary, Firefox Nightly and Safari Technology Preview.

D2: For a shadow host with `delegatesFocus` whose focused area is a scrollable region, "get the focusable area" returns the region's DOM anchor instead of the region. The new "is the currently focused area" check then never matches, so a second `host.focus()` still scrolls. Chrome and Firefox don't scroll; Safari doesn't make the scroller focusable. Not applied: proposed fix, which returns the focused area itself: [spec](https://github.com/mrego/html/pull/1), [test](https://github.com/mrego/wpt/pull/555).

Q1: `focus({ focusVisible })` still runs "indicate focus" when the focus doesn't move. Chrome, Firefox, and Safari all leave `:focus-visible` unchanged when `focus({ focusVisible: true })` or `focus({ focusVisible: false })` is called on the element that already has focus. Should that step also depend on whether the focus moved?
- a: depend on the same condition as scrolling: [spec](https://github.com/mrego/html/pull/2), [test](https://github.com/mrego/wpt/pull/556). This matches all three engines, but widens this PR beyond scrolling.
- b: keep as is here, and file a follow-up issue.

Q2: When the top-level traversable doesn't have system focus, the currently focused area is null. The check never matches, so `focus()` on the element that already has focus still runs the focus update steps, which scroll and fire `focus`. With a popup holding system focus, Firefox and Safari neither scroll nor fire `focus`. Chrome kept system focus under automation, so I couldn't test it there. Open, no fix yet.
- a: compare against the focused area while ignoring system focus. This needs care so that an element that is only its own document's focused area still gets focus, e.g. inside an iframe while the parent has focus elsewhere.
- b: keep as is, and handle it in a separate issue about focus without system focus.

<details><summary>Reviewed commits</summary>

Reviewed at e6adc69 on 823898c, with web-platform-tests/wpt#65371 at b356dcd, using spec-pr-review.
</details>
</details>

> Not applied yet: D1 and D2. Open: Q1 and Q2.

What do the D numbers mean?
